 PROJECTED LINEUP: Oilers vs. Lightning
 View the Oilers projected lines, defence pairings & starting goalie for Thursday's meeting with the Lightning at Benchmark International Arena
 November 19, 2026 
 Link copied 
 TAMPA, FL – As per the lines at Thursday's morning skate, forward Colton Dach is expected to be elevated to the top line with Connor McDavid and Zach Hyman when the Edmonton Oilers face the Tampa Bay Lightning at Benchmark International Arena.
 Head Coach Mike Babcock will look to replicate Tuesday's 5-2 win over the Florida Panthers, the Blue & Orange's sixth straight win, by splitting Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl onto separate lines.
 Leon Draisaitl was between Vasily Podkolzin and Kasperi Kapanen on the second line, as the trio looks to build on their success together, which has seen them outscore opponents 25-8 over the past two seasons when together for a 74 percent goal share.
 As for the rest of the lineup, the Lightning didn't hold a pre-game skate on Thursday, so Babcock is going to be paying close attention during warmups tonight for any last-minute changes that he could make prior to puck drop to combat a deep and skilled Lightning side that's had the Oilers' number in this building over the years by winning 10 of the past 13 meetings (11-1-1).
 Mike speaks to the media prior to Thursday's meeting with the Lightning
 Babcock praised his bottom six after Tuesday's win over the Panthers and hopes to see another impactful performance from them tonight, with the forward group subject to change depending on what he sees during warmups.
 "I've felt this year that lots of times we haven't been able to string together shifts, so that was good for us," he said. "I don't know what I'm going to do tonight. I'm going to watch them warm up. They didn't have a skate today. I'm going to see them all in person there, and then I'll have a better handle on what I'm going to do."
 For forward Dickinson, who's been critical to anchoring Edmonton's third line, he relishes the opportunity to shut down some of the League's best players and will face a stern challenge in the Lightning tonight to help try and keep the win streak going.
 "It's easy to get up for.  This is a challenge that I live for," Dickinson said. "I love to go up against those guys and make their night miserable. My favourite part is seeing them get frustrated, slamming sticks, slamming doors, so that's when you know you've had a good night."
 Goalie Devon Levi is projected to make his 12th start of the season, aiming to win his seventh straight appearance.
 Jason speaks before facing the Lightning in Tampa on Thursday
 View the Oilers Projected Lineup vs. the Lightning below: 
 Dach - McDavid - Hyman
Podkolzin - Draisaitl - Kapanen
Hallander - Dickinson - Frederic
Formenton - Michaels - Joseph
 Ekholm - Bouchard
Shea - Murphy
Mukhamadullin - Emberson 
 Levi
